analysis:
The PR only changes CI runner routing for the build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks lanes, plus comments in .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml (about lines 56-58 and 862-864), a changelog entry and docs/developer/build.md. While job sizes are off, these jobs now ask the Darkbloom route without a size instead of staying on the Blacksmith fallback. No shipped provider runtime code, wire protocol, attestation, App Attest, cache or fan-helper code is touched, so the runtime threat IDs (T-041, T-053, T-054, TB-011 and similar) are unaffected.

I read the supplied workflow tail (lines 520-1231). It has no new behavior: actions are pinned by SHA, checkout uses persist-credentials false, ci-plan-checks and the provider-test-gate are unchanged, and the artifact uploads are unchanged. The job-to-lane mapping lives in provider-plan.yml, which was not supplied, so I could not verify it. The runs-on value still comes from fromJSON(inputs.routes)[lane], so the lane keys named in the comments must still exist in the route output.

Residual CI supply-chain question: the build jobs now run on routed Darkbloom Sandbox Macs rather than fixed Blacksmith runners. Those jobs produce test products (cluster-test-products, provider-test-products) and release-build caches. Whether the routed runners are trusted, ephemeral and isolated, and whether the GitHub Actions cache is safe against poisoning (SAVE_CACHES gates saving to master and dev pushes), depends on provider-plan.yml and the route plane, neither of which was supplied. The build lanes were already routable when sizes were on, so this is not a new capability. The change only widens the situations in which routing applies. This is documented context, not a demonstrated regression, and the threat model scopes CI out. I raise no finding, but a reviewer with provider-plan.yml should confirm that release artifacts are not built or signed on these routed runners without equivalent trust.
